event.summary: Check whether lifecycle confirmation can dispatch a newer session or prompt
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1d24c6af0b6fdbbec854623ff53f90281b8271ab

## TLDR
A sandbox Stop and suspend confirmation may use a later render's session or guards rather than the session the user answered about. This is an unresolved source lead, not an observed failure.

## Details
Controls stores question as Signal<Option<Operation>>; its confirm handler calls execute, a use_callback whose refreshed closure clones execute_session and takes live held/stop_guards (around lines 261-284). It does not use ConfirmSlot. SPEC_impl.md, GUI: Dioxus, Answers bind to what was drawn requires answers to bind to the render and says every destructive prompt uses ConfirmSlot. Need verify component identity and claim lifetime in callers, callback update semantics already used elsewhere in code, and patch scope before deciding if a shipped action can stop the wrong session or consume a newer question. Suggested bucket: high if merely wrong UX; could-be-highest explicitly unresolved because stopping another session's work requires a reachable cross-target route. Confidence: uninvestigated lead. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. No runtime reproduction requested or performed. Evidence packets currently blocked by invalid caller-owned manifest ranges; context source read via git show.

event.summary: Session-only environment deletion retains the caller's scope and approval guards
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 12c79f61a627a4241707dad0cf3b55b859d2d4fc

## TLDR
Considered whether the new session-only deletion helper lets an agent destroy work outside its own environment or bypass approval. Source analysis refutes that route.

## Details
The new helper at sessions.rs:3469 delegates to delete_session_teardown, preserving the connection-id check, approval denial fence, guarded supervisor delete and local cleanup (:3481-3518). Its only caller is agent_requests.rs:2729, selected only for AgentScope::Environment. The Delete dispatch resolves through resolve_scoped_target (:660-671), whose scope.admit_target requires the origin's host (:1435-1445, :399-403), refuses self-deletion (:679-685), reads the live target and derives its DeleteGuard, and awaits approved before dispatch (:2703-2722). Fleet callers retain do_delete_session and its session-owned-host refusal. SPEC.md Agents and environments: 'Deleting another session in the environment removes that session only, through the ordinary session teardown, and never the environment'. The caller and shared teardown meet this contract. Suggested bucket if the suspected bypass existed: highest (unauthorized process/work deletion); could-be-highest: yes, refuted by the caller's shipped checks. Confidence: confirmed source-only. proposed_drop: source refutation at the above scope, approval and connection guards. possible_cover: none. No execution or reproduction.

event.summary: The stale-suspension browser test counts unrelated host reads as its readiness oracle
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: ba7cc0264028eebb39647deb1d25b055e6886935

## TLDR
The browser regression test can report a successful wake without establishing that the launch saw the stale suspension it is supposed to tolerate. A regression in that integration path can therefore escape this test. This is a test-evidence issue, not an observed product failure.

## Details
In the 'stale suspension after the resume' case, :582-585 claims that two /api/hosts reads prove the wake read the intermediate suspension, then :595 immediately publishes Connected. But fleet increments reads for every host response at :79, without identifying the consumer, and snapshots the phase only after route.fetch resolves (:61-77). The independent list reader fetches the same endpoint at list/view.rs:2155, responds to feed notifications at :2328-2333, and queues a follow-up notice behind an in-flight read (:2325-2327; reader.rs module contract). The test's Resume route itself emits a notification via fixture.publishState (:547-552). Nothing waits for the display reader to become idle before setting the count baseline. An in-flight display read plus its queued follow-up can satisfy the two-read threshold before the wake helper's response is constructed; the next helper response then sees Connected directly. api.rs:5736-5741 accepts that response immediately, so this execution never exercises stale-suspension handling. The count also advances before route.fulfill, and therefore proves response preparation rather than consumer processing.

The Test authoring review requires: 'Assert the fixture premise before the action or measurement that depends on it' and 'Assert an observable that distinguishes the competing mechanisms.' Bind the held phase to a wake-owned read/observation, or use an explicit test observation that the wake consumed it before publishing Connected. Existing direct WakeWatch unit tests (api.rs:8918 onward) cover the pure classifier, so this does not claim that the stale-mark rule is wholly untested; the missing evidence is the new browser test's integration premise. Suggested bucket: other (maintainer test quality). Could-be-highest: no. Confidence: confirmed source-level oracle ambiguity; the described interleaving was not executed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: pure classifier unit coverage noted above, no queue sources searched. Revision closes the lead with the actual independent-reader and helper paths checked.

event.summary: The stale-suspension browser test counts unrelated host reads as its readiness oracle
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: ba7cc0264028eebb39647deb1d25b055e6886935

## TLDR
The browser regression test can report a successful wake without establishing that the launch saw the stale suspension it is supposed to tolerate. A regression in that integration path can therefore escape this test. This is a test-evidence issue, not an observed product failure.

## Details
Synthesis rechecked the actual response boundary. fleet constructs each response's rewritten phase at :65-78, after route.fetch and response.json complete (:63-64), then increments the global reads counter at :79 and fulfills that fixed JSON at :86. Changing publishedState after that point cannot alter an already prepared response. Therefore the earlier record's observation that counting precedes fulfill is NOT by itself a failure: if either counted response belongs to the helper, the stale snapshot is already fixed and will exercise it even if delivery/processing happens later. The remaining issue is consumer attribution, not late processing.

The scenario waits for two reads after answered.wait (:581-585), then publishes Connected (:595). Those reads include the independent display owner (list/view.rs:2150-2155) as well as resume_host_connected (api.rs:5718,5736). The display owner starts a mount read and a feed read (list/view.rs:2311-2333). fleet arms a revision-1 greeting (:49); stubFeed sends that greeting on subscription (helpers/fleet.ts:697-700). The Resume route publishes another notice before answering (:555-557). reader.rs:444-456 records a notice behind a currently running read, and :517-535 starts that follow-up when the current read finishes. The test waits for session/terminal readiness (:572-573; attachSession in helpers/term.ts:406-423), not display-host-reader idleness. Thus a revision-1 display read still awaiting route.fetch when the answer baseline is captured, followed by the queued Resume-notice display read, can supply both counted snapshots before the helper's own route.fetch resolves. Connected is then published, and the helper's response is constructed as Connected. Its api.rs:5740-5741 immediately succeeds without passing a stale post-Resume suspension to WakeWatch. This is a source-permitted ordering; no run established its frequency or occurrence.

Meaningful competing failure: integration could initialize/reset the helper's WakeWatch from a post-Resume non-suspended phase instead of the saved pre-Resume suspension. The unchanged classifier would then reject a genuinely delivered stale suspension as SuspendedAgain; if the test's two reads are both display reads and the helper first receives Connected, that integration regression passes. The pure unit tests at api.rs:8918-8929 construct WakeWatch directly with a suspension and therefore do not cover this helper wiring. The parent revision's helper already waits through an ordinary suspension; this report does not claim the new test necessarily misses a particular pre-existing stale-suspension bug.

The Test authoring review requires 'Assert the fixture premise before the action or measurement that depends on it' and 'Assert an observable that distinguishes the competing mechanisms.' Bind readiness to a wake-owned snapshot/observation, or explicitly drain and fence the display reader before relying on request counts. Suggested bucket: other (maintainer test quality). Could-be-highest: no. Confidence: confirmed source-level ambiguity; the false-pass interleaving is source analysis, not execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: direct WakeWatch unit coverage, limited to classifier semantics; no coverage-source searches. This revision narrows the initial finding and preserves its original consequence while correcting the response-processing rationale.

event.summary: Cache-only retirement metadata gap has no established normal serving route
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc

## TLDR
Considered a pin/read metadata write bypass for retired sessions listed only in an identity-less host's memory. The cache-only helper would miss such a synthetic row, but source checks did not establish that ordinary Farhelm serving can produce the required state. Do not report it as a shipped product regression on that premise.

## Details
The conditional mismatch is real in source: refuse_cached_retired at :4538-4546 examines only cached_session; resolve_owner at :936-965 accepts live_sessions membership; mark_seen/set_pin use that cache-only fence, while raise_notification_marks at :3770-3795 explicitly checks live first. Store mark_seen (:6260 onward) and set_pinned (:6370 onward) can write without a session-cache foreign key. SPEC_impl.md:5913-5917 explicitly supports identity-less live-list serving on a row with no recorded identity, so cache absence is not by itself a refutation.

The required production premise was then checked at the supervisor, rather than inferred from the manager's accepted wire shape. core.rs:6587-6591 always ensures Some(host identity) when it holds state-dir ownership. Only a claimless construction can read None (docs :4985-4999, construction :6529-6555). Actual serve at :8483-8505 refuses unless ownership exists and begin_serving succeeds; normal startup at :18898 uses that constructor then serving path. A pre-identity old supervisor cannot supply this same-protocol row: manager.rs:4367-4371 explicitly notes the older protocol is refused before this branch. Identity-less test peers/direct connection harnesses can exercise the manager shape, but no ordinary source route combines a legitimate persisted retired container session with an identity-less serving supervisor. UI automatic seen admission also excludes retired rows (session_view.rs:3405-3409), and retired row menus/drag controls are filtered (list/row.rs:1352,1381,5116 onward); no shipped GUI metadata emitter established this bypass independently.

Suggested bucket for the original conditional metadata-only effect: other. Could-be-highest: false, no security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed cache/live conditional distinction and normal-serving identity fence; no runtime evidence. proposed_drop: no established shipped premise after checking real constructor, serve gate, protocol compatibility and GUI emitters. This is not a claim that an arbitrary custom peer cannot send an identity-less retired-looking row, nor that supported live-list semantics cease to matter elsewhere. possible_cover: none in supplied neighbours. Revision closes the lead as a candidate; no unresolved investigation is retained.
